title: canary-stochasticity-calibration-and-ops-notebook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an experimental, operational-first approach to canarying LLM-powered routes where output stochasticity (generation variance) is a first-order signal. Goal: reduce false positives from behavioral noise while preserving sensitivity to real regressions introduced by model or routing changes.

Scope / when to use this notebook:
- Small surface experiments (feature flags and model variant swaps) that modify sampling, temperature, or model checkpoints.
- Not intended for full traffic migration or major architecture changes (those need full release playbooks).
- Useful when we expect signal to be subtle and stochastic (e.g., ranking changes, reranker deltas, paraphrase drift).

High-level approach (one-liner):
Drive canaries with paired-sample comparisons + ensemble baseline + noise calibration windows.

Hypotheses to validate in each run:
- H1: Metric drift beyond expected stochastic envelope implies deployment regression.
- H2: Short-term spikes in behavioral metrics (e.g., hallucination label) that decay within noise window are noise, not regressions.
- H3: Prefix/KV-cache interactions can create correlated bursts; need stratified slicing.

Metrics (primary / secondary):
- Primary: user-facing quality metric aligned to product (e.g., rerank-CTR-lift, helpfulness-score).
- Statistical: paired-difference mean, confidence interval using bootstrap (paired by request id).
- Noise envelope: rolling stddev of paired diffs across baseline-window (configurable window size, default 3h).
- Secondary telemetry: median latency P95, token-level cost, server error rate, model fallback rate, human-review flags.
- Safety signals: hallucination-rate, toxicity-rate, PII-detection-count.

Sampling / cohort design:
- Always do paired-sample where possible: same request hashed to variant A and B in short succession (within N seconds) to reduce context drift.
- Cohorts: new-users-only, returning-users-only, heavy-token sessions, mobile vs desktop, geographic regions.
- Microcohort gating: start with 0.1% traffic, increase to 1% -> 5% -> 20% by time-based gates + signal gates.
- Randomization seed transparency: record seed in logs for reproducibility.

Calibration window and noise model:
- Calibration period: first 24h after deployment where we measure baseline stochasticity of key metrics for the model pair.
- Establish noise envelope: median +/- 2.5 * MAD (robust) or use bootstrap CI of paired diffs.
- If observed delta lies inside envelope, treat as noise. If outside AND sustained across 3 contiguous windows (default 1h windows), escalate.

Statistical tests and rules of thumb:
- Use paired bootstrap CI (10k resamples) on mean difference. Prefer median difference for heavy-tailed metrics.
- Threshold for action: lower bound of CI > pre-set improvement threshold OR upper bound < pre-set degradation threshold. For safety metrics, any increase above baseline by X% is immediate flag (X configurable per metric).
- Avoid p-value hunting — rely on effect size + operational significance.

Abort and rollback conditions (ordered):
1) Safety-first: any high-severity safety signal (PII extraction, major hallucination for finance/legal personas) -> immediate 100% rollback + pager.
2) Latency SLO breach: sustained P95 > SLO for 2 consecutive measurement windows (default 10m windows) -> auto-revert.
3) Cost surge: >2x token cost/unit for sustained 30m -> alert, manual check (could be due to sampling param bug).
4) Quality regression: primary metric drop lower-bound CI crosses negative-degradation-threshold for 3 contiguous windows OR human-review rate doubles.

Observability contract (what must be shipped with any canary):
- Tagged tracing spans that include rollout-id, variant-id, random-seed, model-checkpoint, sampling params.
- Per-request logged metrics (hashed request id, cohort tag, latency, token-count, model-output-hash, safety-flags). No customer data in logs — scrub before storage.
- Dashboards: paired-diff timeseries, ensemble baseline band, cohort breakdown, alert timeline.
- Automated synthetic probes that exercise edge-case prompts (run every 15m) with deterministic seeds.

Runbook (operator steps):
Pre-deploy checks (must complete):
- Confirm rollout config in Console: variants, weights, duration, rollback policy.
- Smoke tests from synthetic-probe suite pass locally and in staging.
- Telemetry contract validated: tracing tags present in canary build.
- Notify stakeholders via release channel and fill the release-comment template.

Deployment sequence:
1) Activate canary at 0.1% with paired-sample enabled.
2) Monitor calibration window metrics for 1h. If no alerts and drift within envelope, move to 1% after 60m.
3) At each step (1% -> 5% -> 20%) verify paired-diff CI and safety signals for at least 2 windows before advancing.
4) If any intermediate gate trips, pause and run quick internal audit (sample outputs, human review).
5) After 20% and 24h of stability, prepare for ramp-to-100% with final stakeholder signoff.

Canary output review checklist (sample):
- Pull 100 recent paired request pairs where diffs exceed 2*sigma.
- For each, record: prompt, both outputs, sampling params and seed, whether KV-cache likely present, reviewer judgement (OK/regression/unknown).
- If >5% labeled regression by human reviewers, trigger rollback.

Human-in-loop / adjudication:
- We need a lightweight adjudication UI where reviewers can see paired outputs and tag with quick labels. Prioritize privacy and redact PII.
- On-call rotations: product+eng steward (1h response SLA) during first 24h high-sensitivity ramp.

Edge cases and heuristics (notes to self):
- Long-tail prompts: sample-based experiments undercount failure modes; we need synthetic stress suites targeted at those types.
- Cache-warmup effects: initial latency/cost spikes can be benign — track warmup-tagged requests separately.
- Model seed exposure: be explicit about exposing seed for reproducibility but strip before customer-visible storage.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default calibration window for low-traffic routes (3 days?).
- Add small-run power analysis HARDCODE? who owns? (Rashmi to run quick sims).
- Integrate auto-labeler for hallucination proxies: build in feature or use external tool? (Diego investigating)
- Who will steward the human-review queue during weekend rollouts? (ops rota gap)

Action items:
- Priya: draft release-comment template + notify checklist (due 2025-11-22).
- Rashmi: simulate calibration windows for 5 synthetic routes and share numbers (due 2025-11-25).
- Liam: hook paired-bootstrap implementation into rollout-utils PR (GITHUB:189) and add unit tests (due 2025-11-28).
- Diego: prototype minimal adjudication UI and redaction flow (due 2025-12-05).

Appendix: quick formulas and defaults
- Default micro-gates: [0.1%, 1%, 5%, 20%]
- Window size: 1h (default), calibration-window: 24h
- Bootstrap resamples: 10,000
- Noise threshold for action: paired-diff outside median +/- 2.5*MAD OR CI lower-bound < -delta (delta set per-metric)

Endnotes / references:
- See CONFLUENCE:Rollouts/Telemetry-Contracts for schema
- Related: JIRA-4827 (canary-runbook-improvements)
- Slack thread: #canary-ops-thread-234 for recent incidents and notes
